title.narrative: The sixth general capital increase of the African Development Bank

description.narrative:
Based on the AfDB’s Annual Development Effectiveness Review, the following results can be reported in relation to select Danish priorities as set out in the Organisation Strategy – for all African countries and for ADF countries, respectively.
Climate change and green growth: Improved ‘access to electricity’, and ‘installed renewable capacity’, as well as ‘access to at least basic drinking water services’, while the latter is still below its 2015 baseline.
‘Access to electricity’: all African Countries: up from 54 to 56 %. ADF: down from 42 to 41 %.
‘Installed renewable capacity’: all African countries: up from 46 to 54 GW. ADF: up from 24 to 26 GW.
‘Access to at least basic drinking water services’: all African countries: up from 66 to 69 %. ADF: up from 56 to 59 %.
Inclusive development and job creation for youth: Unchanged for ‘population living below the poverty line’, while ‘youth unemployment rate’ and correspondingly for ‘young women’ increased.
‘Population living below the poverty line’: all African countries: remained at 34 %. ADF: down from 42 to 36 %.
‘Youth unemployment rate’: all African countries: up from 14 to 16 %; young women: up from 17 to 20 %. ADF: up from 8 to 10 %; young women: up from 9 to 11 %.
Fragility: Increased number of refugees and internally displaced people. All African countries: up from 29 to 33 million. ADF: up from 25.2 to 29.2 million.
Gender equality: The ‘Gender Inequality Index’ remained at 0.52 for all African countries and 0.57 for ADF on a scale from 0-1 (low-high).
Sources Annual Development Effectiveness Review 2022 Strategy for Denmark’s Engagement with the African Development Bank 2020-2024
Link to annual reports from 2016-2023: 2016: file://u1.um.dk/data/home/livhvi/Downloads/afdb_annual_report_2016_en.pdf 2017: https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/document/afdb-annual-report-2017-101996 2018: https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/annual-report-2018 2019: https://www.afdb.org/en/documen

The significant lending provided during the global financial crisis significantly hollowed out the capacity of the African Development Bank (AfDB) to take loans from international capital markets. Without the influx of capital, the level of activities of AfDB would have decreased dramatically by 2012. In May 2010, AfDB's Board of Governors therefore agreed upon a 200 % extension of capital, of which 6 % were to be disbursed, while the rest stands as guaranteed capital.
The extension of capital increases the economic latitude of the Bank's "hard window", where AfDB lends money to creditworthy middle-income countries and finances all of its investments in the private sector. Almost half of these investments are directed towards businesses in African low-income countries. Its strategic and operational priorities are aligned with those of the African Development Bank Group's Ten Year Strategy for 2013-2022, which two overall objectives are inclusive and green growth. The Strategy determines the AfDB¿s strategic selectivity and operational focus on infrastructure, regional integration, private sector development, governance and accountability, and skills and technology; with three areas of special emphasis namely fragile states, food security and agriculture, and gender. These objectives are well in line with overall Danish development priorities.
